correctness.rationale: Cells of the AB hemisphere are exactly joined pairs of factor words, and the BA hemisphere is its opposite join. Their intersection is precisely the disjoint union of connected factor word complexes. Both embeddings of this intersection into either join are nullhomotopic, so the homotopy pushout splits as two copies of the join plus the unreduced suspension of the disjoint union, which is a circle plus two individual suspensions. The Farmer/Björner–Wachs full-word sphere theorem gives the derangement counts. The standalone finite-field boundary checker passed 234 factor pairs in both characteristics and reproduced three full-block Betti vectors, without being substituted for the general homotopy proof.

originality.rationale: The asserted universal two-family, two-block-order unstable wedge decomposition and its full-block wreath-group sphere formula are not stated by the inspected primary papers. Govc proves a free fundamental group but no explicit reversal formula; Chacholski–Levi–Meshulam give individual-permutation and separate join/concatenation tools, not the union of both block orders for arbitrary factors. The 2026 pattern-avoiding shellability results concern a different generating rule. Distinct indexed cyclic/dihedral permutation-complex records concern rotations/reversals of one word and cannot imply this arbitrary-factor construction. Novelty is relative to actual searched sources, not guaranteed against unindexed literature.
residual_risks: The result uses standard homotopy-pushout and join machinery; an equivalent specialized block-order formula may exist under another name outside searchable indices.

The two highly relevant cyclic/reversal indexed summaries were compared at statement level, not their complete documents; the generator families differ and their displayed statements do not dominate this result.

value.rationale: This is an exact, reusable unstable homotopy operation on any two permutation complexes, not a calculation of an arbitrary small example. It shows how to build complexes retaining a universal infinite-cyclic fundamental group while independently carrying suspensions of both input homotopy types and two copies of their join. Its two-parameter full-block specialization exactly classifies the natural imprimitive wreath-product family in every size, giving mixed sphere degrees and integral multiplicities via derangements. The result supplies a concrete constructive mechanism beyond the previously known qualitative free-fundamental-group theorem and two-individual-permutation case.
